zázhì — "magazine".
wǒ mǎi le liǎng běn zázhì — I bought two magazines.
Its characters come later; for now it is a word for the ear.

zázhì is built from zá 'mixed' and zhì 'a record', both inherited from Middle Chinese, dzop and tsyiH (Guangyun, in Baxter's transcription), which glosses the first 'to gather' and 'five colours together' and the second 'to note down': a record of many things.

报 — bào — "newspaper; the daily paper".
我每天早上看报 wǒ měitiān zǎoshang kàn bào — I read the paper every morning.

The new character, in pieces: 报 (bào) — seven strokes in two pieces: on the left the hand piece of 打, three strokes; on the right a bar that turns down and hooks back, a long vertical down its left side, then a bar that turns into a sweep to the lower left and a long stroke falling to the right. The next lesson puts it in your hand.
报 (bào) is inherited from Middle Chinese pawH (Guangyun, in Baxter's transcription), which glosses it 'to report'; the sense 'a newspaper', the sheet that reports, is later and is not given there.
One more word for telling what happened.

blocks.title: Script — the hand piece, then a hook, a post and a fork

segments.text: 报 (bào).
Two pieces, left before right. Count the pieces, not the strokes.
The left piece, three strokes. The hand piece of 打: a bar, a vertical that hooks to the left at the foot, and a stroke rising to the right across it.

The right piece, four strokes. A bar that turns down and hooks back to the left. A long vertical down the left side of the piece. Then the fork: a bar that turns into a sweep down to the lower left, and a long stroke falling to the right.
3 + 4 = seven.

segments.text: How many pieces in 报 (bào)? (Two.) What is the left piece? (The hand piece of 打, three strokes.) What closes the right piece? (A fork: a sweep to the left, then a long stroke to the right.)

segments.text: 见报 — jiànbào — "to appear in the papers; to make the papers".
我们学校见报了 wǒmen xuéxiào jiànbào le — Our school was in the paper.

见报 (jiànbào) is built from 见 'to see' and 报 (bào) 'a newspaper', both inherited from Middle Chinese, kenH and pawH (Guangyun, in Baxter's transcription), which glosses the first 'to view': to be seen in the paper.
One more word for telling what happened.

tóutiáo is built from 头 'the head' and tiáo 'a strip', both inherited from Middle Chinese, duw and dew (Guangyun, in Baxter's transcription), which glosses the first 'the head' and the second 'a small branch': the first strip, the story at the top.

guānzhù — "to follow a story closely; to keep an eye on".
rúguǒ nǐ guānzhù xīnwén, nǐ jiù huì zhīdào — If you followed the news, you'd know.
Its characters come later; for now it is a word for the ear.

guānzhù is built from 关 'to shut' and zhù 'to pour', both inherited from Middle Chinese, kwaen and tsyuH (Guangyun, in Baxter's transcription), which glosses the first 'the bar that holds a gate shut' and the second 'to pour into'; how the pair came to mean 'to follow closely' is not settled.
One more word for telling what happened.
